item.title: Siemens Mendix Studio Pro
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Mendix Studio Pro contains multiple vulnerabilities in the MCP Server, that could allow an attacker with network access to interact with the server remotely or trick a user's browser into sending unauthorized requests, potentially leading to unauthorized data access, tool execution, or system compromise. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.

The following versions of Siemens Mendix Studio Pro are affected:

  • Mendix Studio Pro 11 vers:intdot/>=11.15.0|<11.16.0 (CVE-2026-112136, CVE-2026-112137)
  • Mendix Studio Pro 11.12 vers:intdot/>=11.12.6|<11.12.7 (CVE-2026-112136, CVE-2026-112137)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 8.8 Siemens Mendix Studio Pro 11
2 Vulnerabilities
Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address, Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Energy
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-112136
The affected products MCP Server does not properly restrict its HTTP listener to the loopback interface, leaving it potentially exposed to remote systems. This could allow an attacker with network access to interact with the MCP Server remotely.
Read More

2 Affected Products

Mendix Studio Pro 11 >= V11.15.0 < V11.16.0

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
Maintain strict inbound firewall policies (such as Windows Defender Firewall) blocking external traffic on port 7782. This is already the case by default on standard Windows installations. If remote access is required, restrict traffic via a secure, authenticated channel (e.g., a VPN or SSH tunnel) rather than opening direct inbound firewall rules.

Vendor fix
Update to V11.16.0 or later version

Mendix Studio Pro 11.12 >= V11.12.6 < V11.12.7

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
Maintain strict inbound firewall policies (such as Windows Defender Firewall) blocking external traffic on port 7782. This is already the case by default on standard Windows installations. If remote access is required, restrict traffic via a secure, authenticated channel (e.g., a VPN or SSH tunnel) rather than opening direct inbound firewall rules.

Vendor fix
Update to V11.12.7 or later version

Relevant CWE: CWE-1327 Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address

CVE-2026-112137
The affected products MCP Server does not properly validate Content-Type and Origin headers on incoming HTTP requests, leaving it vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). This could allow a malicious web page to trick a user's browser into sending unauthorized requests and executing unintended actions on the local MCP Server.

Mendix Studio Pro 11 >= V11.15.0 < V11.16.0

Product Status: known_affected

Utilize modern Chromium- or WebKit-based browsers with Private Network Access protections enabled, or use browser extensions (such as uBlock Origin or NoScript) to block external websites from issuing fetch requests to localhost (127.0.0.1).

General Recommendations

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity

Additional Resources

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

item.title: Dorsett Controls InfoScan
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to retrieve sensitive system information, access application data without authorization, recover stored credentials, or intercept and manipulate network communications.

The following versions of Dorsett Controls InfoScan are affected:

  • InfoScan <=1.45.0 (CVE-2026-117659, CVE-2026-120157, CVE-2026-120255, CVE-2026-120260, CVE-2026-120271, CVE-2026-120298)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 8.1 Dorsett Controls InfoScan
5 Vulnerabilities
Improper Certificate Validation, Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere, Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key, Missing Authentication for Critical Function, Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Water and Wastewater Systems
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: United States

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-117659
The InfoScan Electron desktop client improperly handles TLS certificate errors by accepting certificates without validating their trustworthiness. The client also configures Electron with nodeIntegration enabled, contextIsolation disabled, and webSecurity disabled. These settings weaken the client’s security boundaries. An attacker who is able to intercept or manipulate network communications may be able to present an untrusted certificate without the application rejecting the connection.
Read More

1 Affected Product

Dorsett Controls InfoScan <=1.45.0

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Dorsett Controls recommends updating affected versions of InfoScan to v1.46 or higher. To install the security patch, user administrators will need to log in to InfoScan and select System Maintenance from the menu. Once the System Maintenance application is open, select Check for Updates, and click the Install Now button in the Ready To Install section. If you are an offline customer (InfoScan has no internet access), you will need to download the update from the Dorsett Controls Customer Portal by selecting the InfoScan Update tile, downloading the update, and following the instructions listed on the portal.

In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

item.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description:
CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. 

  • CVE-2024-10441 Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-40217 BerriAI LiteLLM Unprotected Alternate Channel Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-90436 Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-90817 Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. 

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. 

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. 

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

item.description:
Country: Cameroon
Sources: Christian Blind Mission, Presbyterian Church, Welthungerhilfe

Please refer to the attached file.

This plan by WHH Anticipatory Humanitarian Action Facility (WAHAFA) partners Christian Blind Mission (CBM) and the Presbyterian Church in Cameroon (PCC) shows how Anticipatory Action supports flood-prone communities in Limbe, Fako Division, Cameroon, to act before severe riverine flooding occurs.

This locally developed Anticipatory Action Plan (AAP) combines rainfall forecasts and community observations to trigger early actions addressing health risks, property damage, displacement and food insecurity. Developed with communities, local authorities and organizations of persons with disabilities, the AAP includes drainage clearance, early warning communication and the distribution of water purification tablets, hygiene supplies, mosquito nets and food items.

Using a two-phase trigger mechanism based on forecasts from the National Observatory on Climate Change (ONACC) and local observations of soil saturation, the AAP enables the activation of anticipatory actions with a lead time of approximately 3-9 days and the release of pre-agreed finance from the WAHAFA Fuel funding.

item.title: Sudan - Concept of Operations, October 2026
item.description:
Country: Sudan
Sources: Logistics Cluster, World Food Programme

Please refer to the attached file.

Content

Background

Since the outbreak of conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in April 2023, Sudan has faced one of the world’s largest humanitarian crises. Nearly 8.9 million people are internally displaced – including more than 6.6 million displaced since the conflict began. This represents a 23 percent decrease from the peak of almost 11.6 million recorded in January 2025, reflecting increased returns, particularly to Khartoum and Al Jazirah. Nearly 4.6 million people have fled to neighbouring countries. The crisis has also exacerbated the humanitarian situation in Chad and South Sudan, both of which were already dealing with protracted emergencies.

In 2026, 33.7 million people in Sudan require humanitarian assistance – an increase of 3.3 million from 2025. Despite these overwhelming needs, access constraints, bureaucratic and administrative impediments, an overstretched logistics market, storage constraints, and rising costs for logistics services continue to hinder the delivery of humanitarian assistance to affected populations. Crossline and cross-border movement of humanitarian personnel and supplies continue to face significant obstacles.

To address these logistical challenges and mitigate disruptions to the humanitarian supply chain, the Logistics Cluster has been scaling up its operations since 2023 (following its initial activation in 2020). With the main operational cell based in Port Sudan, the Logistics Cluster leads coordination, advocates for the uninterrupted flow of assistance, and supports humanitarian partners operating across the country.

Operational Constraints

Humanitarian organizations are facing significant operational challenges due to factors including movement restrictions, airspace closures, limited safe access to conflict-affected areas, complex deconfliction processes, bureaucratic impediments, and telecommunications constraints, among others. These issues are significantly hindering the delivery of assistance to affected populations.

Partners have reported the following logistics gaps and bottlenecks impacting their operations, including through the Gaps and Needs Analysis (GNA) published in August 2025:

  • Limited humanitarian access to hard-to-reach areas, particularly in Darfur and Kordofan regions.
  • Limited operational points of entry into Sudan and restrictions on crossline movements due to ongoing conflict and insecurity.
  • Limited ability to contract reliable transportation and storage services due to security constraints, an overstretched market, rising costs, and service disruptions.
  • Insufficient temperature-controlled storage and transport capacity, particularly for cross-border corridors.
  • Limited information on logistics service providers’ availability and capacity, market conditions, and road network and infrastructure status, particularly during the rainy season.
  • Bureaucratic and administrative impediments, including lengthy and frequently changing customs and importation procedures and travel permit approval delays.
  • Airspace closure except for limited air access in Port Sudan, Khartoum, Kassala, and Dongola.
  • Limited fuel availability and rising costs in certain areas.

For detailed and up-to-date information on ports, airports, border crossings, and other logistics infrastructure, partners are encouraged to consult the Sudan Logistics Capacity Assessment (LCA).

El Niño conditions are underway and are forecasted to strengthen through late 2026, coinciding with a strong positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD).

Key Messages

Seasonal forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of below-normal rainfall, prolonged dry spells and above-normal temperatures, while above-normal rainfall and flooding risks are expected in parts of the northern areas of the region.

The region remains highly vulnerable following the severe 2023/24 El Niño, which affected an estimated 54.4 million people and contributed to widespread food insecurity, livelihood losses and disease outbreaks. Currently, humanitarian needs remain elevated, with 11 million acutely food insecure people across the region, while funding levels remain low.

III. Southern Africa experienced one of its largest cholera outbreaks during 2024-25, increasing public health concerns entering the 2026/27 El Niño season.

IV. Governments and partners are advancing contingency planning, preparedness and anticipatory action measures to reduce the expected impacts on food security, water resources, livelihoods, health and protection during the 2026/27 season.

V. Critical funding gaps in preparedness and anticipatory action are undermining efforts to protect vulnerable communities from the expected impacts of El Niño.

item.title: Ecuador: ENOS - Lluvia e inundaciones - Flash Update No. 02 (al 17 de noviembre 2026)
item.description:
Country: Ecuador
Source: UN Country Team in Ecuador

Please refer to the attached file.

DESTACADOS

  • Según cifras oficiales, desde el 29 de agosto de 2026, las lluvias asociadas al fenómeno de El Niño han dejado más de 80.000 personas impactadas y afectaciones a 166 cantones y 508 parroquias, con predominio de inundaciones (57%) y deslizamientos (17%).
  • Los pronósticos del Comité Nacional para el Estudio Regional del Fenómeno El Niño (CN-ERFEN) y del Centro Internacional para la Investigación del Fenómeno de El Niño (CIIFEN) indican que El Niño continúa fortaleciéndose y podría alcanzar una intensidad fuerte a muy fuerte entre finales de 2026 e inicios de 2027, aumentando el riesgo de lluvias intensas, inundaciones y crecidas de ríos, particularmente en la región Costa.
  • Las evaluaciones preliminares realizadas en territorios afectados identifican necesidades prioritarias en alojamiento, agua, saneamiento e higiene, salud, seguridad alimentaria, protección y recuperación temprana, especialmente entre hogares que han sufrido daños en sus viviendas y pérdida de bienes esenciales.
  • El Gobierno mantiene la Alerta Roja nacional por el fenómeno de El Niño y coordina la respuesta a través de 215 Comités de Operaciones de Emergencias (en adelante COE) activos, mientras que la asistencia humanitaria entregada supera los 60.000 bienes de ayuda distribuidos por la SNGR y las instituciones del Sistema Nacional Descentralizado de Gestión Integral de Riesgos y Desastres (en adelante SNDGIRD).(34.130 por La Secretaría Nacional de Gestión de Riesgos- SNGR y 26.794 por el SNDGIRD).

RESUMEN DE LA SITUACIÓN

Las lluvias asociadas al fortalecimiento del fenómeno de El Niño continúan generando afectaciones en Ecuador. Desde el 29 de agosto hasta el 17 de noviembre de 2026, según cifras oficiales, se han registrado al menos 83.975 personas impactadas (51.095 afectadas y 32.880 damnificadas), además, se reportan 1.500 eventos adversos relacionados con precipitaciones en las 24 provincias, afectando a 166 cantones y 508 parroquias. Las inundaciones representan el 57% de los eventos reportados, seguidas por deslizamientos (17%), lluvias intensas (7%) y vendavales (6%). Las provincias con mayor impacto en la población son Esmeraldas, Guayas, El Oro, Los Ríos, Santa Elena, Manabí, Galápagos y Bolívar.

De acuerdo con el Comité Nacional para el Estudio Regional del Fenómeno El Niño (CN-ERFEN), las condiciones oceánicas y atmosféricas continúan mostrando el fortalecimiento del evento, con una probabilidad superior al 83% de que alcance una intensidad fuerte a muy fuerte durante los próximos meses. Este escenario coincide con los análisis del Centro Internacional para la Investigación del Fenómeno de El Niño (CIIFEN), que identifica el periodo entre octubre y diciembre de 2026 como la fase de mayor intensidad del fenómeno, aumentando el riesgo de lluvias por encima de lo normal, inundaciones y crecidas de ríos en la región Costa.

En respuesta al incremento de las afectaciones, las autoridades nacionales y locales han fortalecido las acciones de preparación y respuesta, incluyendo la activación de mecanismos de coordinación de emergencia, la emisión de alertas y declaratorias correspondientes, así como la movilización de asistencia humanitaria para las poblaciones afectadas. De manera paralela, las instituciones del sistema nacional de gestión de riesgos mantienen el monitoreo de las condiciones hidrometeorológicas y de la evolución del fenómeno de El Niño, con el fin de anticipar impactos y ampliar las capacidades de respuesta en los territorios de mayor exposición.
